  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_latest_hold` picks the newest hold by `created_at`, and a manual resume does not close it, so a re-blocked item finds the old open hold.
  WHY: The judge refreshes the old hold comment and returns without deciding, so the re-blocked item gets no decision for up to 14 days.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:329-334 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `git grep` result no longer decides the hold condition (exit codes 0 and 1 are treated alike), yet it scans the whole checkout on every hold check, and an exit code of 2 or higher returns `unknown` before the variable/secret check.
  WHY: This adds wasted I/O on every tick, and a grep error blocks the API check that would otherwise return `met`. Reviewers' severity was NIT, mapped to low.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:4072-4099 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The Claude Code footer exemption in `_is_unrouted_non_human_body` checks only that the text starts with "/", while `is_reclarify_command_body` also accepts `/reclarify` on a later line, so such a comment is treated as non-human and never flagged as unrouted. Anthropic and Gemini raised this only as a hardening suggestion.
  WHY: A footer-bearing comment with a later-line `/reclarify` that fails to route goes undetected, and the new test covers only the leading `/reclarify`. Reviewers' severity was NIT, mapped to low.
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:170-174 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `placeholder_retired` semantics changed, so any caller that relied on "missing from code means met" will now hang.
  WHY: This is an intentional, documented behavior break noted only as a heads-up. Reviewer's severity was NIT, mapped to low.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1613,1725 (also 269) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A `placeholder_retired` hold can be met only by an Actions variable or secret, but the hold comments still say the judge resumes the item once the step is done, and the manual-resume instruction is only in `changelog.d/8287-operator-step-hold-docs-only-placeholder.md`.
  WHY: The judge reports "unmet" on every run and refreshes the comment until UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS (14 days) without posting a resume command. The tests check only the log line `outcome=holding`, not the comment text.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:250-262,1677-1733 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `unblock_latest_hold` chooses the latest hold by `created_at` only, and the hold stays open until the judge marks it done or expired, so a manual resume does not close it.
  WHY: A re-blocked item finds the old open `placeholder_retired` hold, and the judge refreshes it and returns without deciding until 14 days after the original hold was created. The reviewer did not verify whether another component closes holds on a manual resume.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:329-334 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The grep result decides nothing, since exit codes 0 and 1 are treated alike, but the grep still scans the whole checkout on every hold check.
  WHY: A grep error with exit 2 or higher returns `unknown` even when the variable/secret check at lines 338-343 would return `met`. `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` would do the same check without the scan.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:4099 (`_is_unrouted_non_human_body`) | risk score=1
  PROBLEM: The slash-command exception checks only the opening of the comment, while `is_reclarify_command_body` (line 4072) also accepts a later-line `/reclarify`.
  WHY: A footer note carrying a later-line `/reclarify` is classed as non-human and never flagged. Suggested fix: append `and not is_reclarify_command_body(text)` (1 line).
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:320-340 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A retired operator step is determined by whether an Actions variable or secret exists, but the hold comments still tell operators the judge resumes automatically, which is no longer true for docs-only steps.
  WHY: Operators wait up to 14 days (UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS) because the condition is never met for docs-only steps.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh (not in the diff hunk; `unblock_latest_hold`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `unblock_latest_hold` picks only the newest trusted hold marker by `created_at`, so manual resumes do not close the hold and a re-block after `/reclarify` sees the old open hold.
  WHY: The judge refreshes the old hold comment and returns without deciding, leaving the re-blocked item without a decision for up to 14 days.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:329 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `git grep` scan still runs on every hold check even though its exit code is ignored and it no longer decides the hold condition.
  WHY: It adds unnecessary I/O on every judge tick.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:4099 (`_is_unrouted_non_human_body`) | risk score=1
  PROBLEM: The Claude Code footer check does not account for a comment that carries the footer and a slash command on a later line, so an interactive session's own slash command could go unflagged.
  WHY: Suggested fix: add `and not is_reclarify_command_body(text)` to the condition (1 line).
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1725 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The hold comment says "the unblock judge resumes this item afterwards", but for a docs-only `placeholder_retired` step the judge cannot resume on its own, because `unblock_hold_condition` returns `met` only when an Actions variable or secret exists (lines 338-343). The correct instruction is only in `changelog.d/8287-operator-step-hold-docs-only-placeholder.md` and `README.md`.
  WHY: The operator waits while the comment is patched with the same wording every UNBLOCK_JUDGE_RETRY_HOURS until the hold expires after 14 days, with no signal that action is needed.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:250-262 (call sites 1677, 1680, 1686-1688) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `unblock_latest_hold` selects the newest hold by `created_at` and never checks for a manual resume, so a hold stays `state=open` after the operator posts `/reclarify`; the `unmet` arm at line 1723 then patches the comment and returns without deciding.
  WHY: The item is stuck for up to 14 days from the original hold's creation, and the hold flips to `done` only when `unblock_hold_condition` returns `met`, which never happens for docs-only steps.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:329-333 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `git grep` no longer decides anything, yet any exit code other than 0 or 1 (for example 2 for a real git error) returns `unknown` before the variable/secret API check at lines 338-343, and the full grep still runs on every hold check.
  WHY: An unrelated git failure on `TARGET_DIR` turns the hold check into `unknown` and delays resumption by UNBLOCK_JUDGE_RETRY_HOURS instead of letting the API check answer.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:4099 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A comment with the Claude Code footer and a mid-body `/reclarify` (no leading slash) is classified as non-human before `is_reclarify_command_body` (lines 4072-4083) is consulted, so no "command_unrouted" flag is raised.
  WHY: The mid-body `/reclarify` is silently ignored, and the new `test_unrouted_ignores_claude_code_status_notes` covers only the leading `/reclarify` plus footer.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:329 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The grep result is discarded by the following `case`, but the grep still runs over the whole default-branch checkout on every hold check.
  WHY: This wastes CPU on every tick, which is not significant on small repositories.
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:170-174 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `placeholder_retired` semantics changed and the HOLD_KINDS docstring now reflects the new behavior, so any caller that depended on "missing from code means met" will now hang.
  WHY: The PR description acknowledges this trade-off, so it is a documented intentional break, noted as a heads-up only.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:4099 | risk score=3
  PROBLEM: A footer comment with a mid-body `/reclarify` is dropped before `is_reclarify_command_body` is consulted.
  WHY: Suggested fix: append `and not is_reclarify_command_body(text)` (1 line).
- HARDENING: scripts/unblock_judge.sh:329 | risk score=3
  PROBLEM: The grep is dead work, and any exit code other than 0 or 1 turns the answer into `unknown` and skips the API check that decides the hold.
  WHY: Suggested fix: delete the grep and the `case` block at lines 329-333 (about -5 lines), keeping the `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` guard at line 319.
- HARDENING: scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1725 | risk score=3
  PROBLEM: The comment misleads operators about who resumes the item for docs-only steps.
  WHY: Suggested fix: branch the comment text on the hold kind so `placeholder_retired` tells the operator to post the resume command or set the placeholder as a variable/secret (about 6 lines).
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:334-343,1723-1730 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A docs-only operator step stays unmet unless a repository Actions variable or secret with the placeholder name exists, but the hold refresh comment says the judge will resume the item after the step is done.
  WHY: Completing a docs-only step, such as fixing labels, does not meet the condition at lines 338-343, so the judge keeps refreshing the hold. The changelog's manual-resume instructions do not appear in the comment.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:250-260,1677-1730 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The hold lookup does not treat a person's manual resume command as ending an open hold; it selects the newest trusted hold marker and uses its state.
  WHY: After a manual resume, a later block still finds the prior hold open, and the judge refreshes it and returns without deciding until the hold expires.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:4072-4083,4099,4165-4196 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The Claude Code footer exemption checks only whether the comment starts with `/`, while `is_reclarify_command_body` also recognizes `/reclarify` on a later line.
  WHY: A footer-bearing status comment with a later-line `/reclarify` is excluded as non-human at line 4165, so the unrouted-reply detector will not flag it if clarification fails to route.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
